author: 5kO0
content:
Implemented (this session). 5-line fix exactly as the audit predicted.

Code change in proto-blue-lex-cbor/src/encoding.rs::cbor_to_lex (the Float arm, ~line 167):

Before: accepted ciborium::Value::Float(f) and silently coerced f.fract() == 0.0 cases to LexValue::Integer(f as i64). Per dag-cbor spec, integers MUST be encoded as CBOR integer types (major types 0/1), never as floats — a float-encoded integer is a wire-format spec violation. Silently coercing it laundered bad input through the decoder.

After: ANY ciborium::Value::Float(_) returns CborError::FloatNotSupported. No fract-check leniency. Strict-by-construction.

Strict `decode()` already caught this case via re-encode canonical-form mismatch, but `decode_lenient()` is also pub — and a permissive cbor_to_lex would silently accept the bad input there. Audit-grep confirmed `decode_lenient` has zero external callers in the workspace today (only used inside lex-cbor's own `decode()` path), so this is purely future-proofing the public surface against bear-trap usage.

Tests added (2):
  - rejects_float_encoded_integer_on_lenient_path: hand-crafts CBOR bytes for f64(5.0) (major type 7, additional info 27, 8-byte float bits). Asserts decode_lenient returns CborError::FloatNotSupported AND strict decode also rejects (with FloatNotSupported propagated through, OR NonCanonical from the canonical-form check — either is correct).
  - rejects_genuine_float: f64(3.5) — locks in that BOTH integral and non-integral floats now flow through the same rejection path.

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo test -p proto-blue-lex-cbor                                 PASS (53 tests across all suites; 2 new)
  cargo build --workspace                                           PASS
  cargo test --workspace                                            PASS (67 suites, 0 failures)
  cargo clippy -p proto-blue-lex-cbor --all-targets -- -D warnings  PASS
  cargo fmt --all --check                                           PASS
  cargo +nightly fuzz run lex_cbor_decode -- -runs=1000             PASS (no crashes; fuzz exercises Float branch among other paths)

Behavioural change: any caller passing CBOR bytes with float-encoded integers through decode_lenient now gets FloatNotSupported instead of a silent coercion to LexValue::Integer. Strict decode behaviour is functionally unchanged (it always rejected via canonical-form mismatch). No existing test relied on the leniency — the previous test suite passed unmodified after the change.

Category: B (local correctness fix) — the architecture stays the same; this site's specific behaviour was wrong; replaced with the strict variant. The audit's strongest-and-most-correct-option (\"reject all floats outright\") was the right call.

The audit's ciborium-leniency claim was nuanced — \"#8 not actually a fix\" because the empirical correctness was already there, but \"#9 is a real bug\" because decode_lenient genuinely accepted spec-violating input. Both parts of that nuance now line up with the current state.
